title: Art and Culture: Musicians (Past Year Questions)

questions.q_en: Who among the following belongs to Patiala Gharana?
questions.solution_en:
The Patiala Gharana of Hindustani classical music was founded in the mid-19th century by Ustad Ali Baksh Khan and his friend Ustad Fateh Ali Khan (who were known as "Aliya-Fattu"). Ali Baksh Khan was the father of the legendary Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, who is one of the most celebrated exponents of this gharana.

Explanation of Other Options:

• Nathu Khan: A sarangi player, possibly associated with various styles but not a founder of Patiala Gharana in the primary sense.

• Abdul Wahid Khan: One of the founders of the Kirana Gharana.

• Chhaju Khan: Associated with the Bhendibazaar Gharana.

Further insights:

• The Patiala Gharana is known for its romantic and expressive style, intricate taans (fast melodic passages), layakari (rhythmic play), and the use of sargams (solfege).

• It incorporates elements from other gharanas like Gwalior, Jaipur, and Kirana.

• Prominent vocalists of this gharana include Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, Ustad Amanat Ali Khan, Ustad Fateh Ali Khan (nephew of Bade Ghulam Ali Khan), Parveen Sultana, and Ajoy Chakrabarty.

questions.q_en: Who among the following established the Indore gharana?
questions.solution_en:
Ustad Amir Khan, a legendary Hindustani classical vocalist, founded the Indore gharana, known for its slow-tempo (vilambit) khayal singing and deep, introspective style.

Explanation of Other Options:

· Bhimsen Joshi: Incorrect, as he was associated with the Kirana gharana.

· Tansen: Incorrect, as Tansen, a 16th-century musician, predates the Indore gharana.

· Ustad Ghaghe Khuda Baksh: Incorrect, as he is not credited with founding the Indore gharana.

questions.q_en: Which of the following is called the cyclic arrangement of time units in Hindustani Classical music?
questions.solution_en:
· Tala refers to the cyclic rhythmic framework in Hindustani classical music.

· Each Tala has a specific number of beats (matras) arranged in groups called vibhags, and these cycles repeat throughout the performance.

· Musicians keep track of the Tala through hand gestures called kriyas (including claps and waves), which mark important points in the rhythmic cycle.

· Examples: Teental (16 beats), Jhaptal (10 beats), Ektaal (12 beats).

Why Not Others?

· Alap: Unmetered, free-flowing melodic introduction.

· Raga: Melodic scale/mood (not time-bound).

· Jati : Classification of ragas or talas by structure.

Key Point: Tala is the metrical cycle that musicians and percussionists (e.g., tabla players) follow.

questions.q_en: With which of the following musical instruments is the musician Zakir Hussain associated?
questions.solution_en:
Ustad Zakir Hussain (born 9 March 1951) is an Indian tabla player, composer, percussionist, music producer and film actor.

He was awarded the Padma shari in 1988, the Padma Bhushan in 2002, and the Padma Vibhushan in 2023, by the Government of India. He was also awarded the Govt of India's Sangeet Natak Academy in 1990, Fellowship of the Sangeet Natak Academy fellowship Ratna Sadsya in 2018.

questions.q_en: Where is the renowned Bhatkhande Music Institute located?
questions.solution_en:
· The renowned Bhatkhande Music Institute is located in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.

· Bhatkhande Music Institute University, formerly known as "Marris College of Hindustani Music" was established by Pt. Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande in July 1926.

· The purpose of its establishment was to liberate music from the monopoly of Gharanedar Musicians and make music education accessible to all.

· The Marris College was established due to the untiring efforts of devoted and dedicated connoisseurs of Art and Musicians like Late Pt. Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande, Late Rai Umanath Bali, Late Raja Nawab Ali Khan and many others.

questions.q_en: Ishwari Prasad is credited to have introduced the ________ Gharana of Kathak.
questions.solution_en: Lucknow Gharana is one of the main gharanas out of the three in Kathak, the other two being Jaipur and Banaras. It represents the lasting Mughal influence on Kathak and was introduced to Lucknow by Maharaj Iswari Prasad Misra and his brothers and further evolved into a court dance over the years.

questions.q_en: Ustad Asad Ali Khan was one of the masters of the ___________.
questions.solution_en:
Ustad Asad Ali Khan (1937 - 2011) was a highly acclaimed Indian musician and one of the foremost exponents of the rudra veena, an ancient plucked string instrument used in Hindustani classical music. He belonged to the Khandarbani dhrupad tradition.

Explanation of Other Options:

· Sarangi: The sarangi is a bowed short-necked string instrument from the Indian subcontinent used in Hindustani classical music.

· Mridangam: The mridangam is a double-sided drum, a primary rhythmic accompaniment in Carnatic music.

· Tanpura: The tanpura (or tambura) is a long-necked plucked string instrument used to provide a continuous harmonic drone in Indian classical music.

Further insights:

· The rudra veena is a large plucked string instrument with a deep, resonant sound, considered one of the oldest and most revered instruments in Indian classical music.

· Ustad Asad Ali Khan was a recipient of several prestigious awards, including the Padma Bhushan (2008) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1977), for his contributions to Indian classical music.

questions.q_en: Bhajan Sopori, a Padma Shri awardee, is a _________ player.
questions.solution_en:
Pandit Bhajan Sopori (1948 - 2022) was a legendary Indian musician and a maestro of the santoor, a stringed musical instrument native to Kashmir. He was a recipient of the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in 2004.

Explanation of Other Options:

• Sitar: A plucked stringed instrument used in Hindustani classical music.

• Tabla: A pair of twin hand drums, the principal percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music.

• Violin: A bowed string instrument, used in both Western classical music and adapted for Indian classical music.

Further insights:

• Bhajan Sopori belonged to the Sufiana gharana of Kashmir and played a significant role in popularizing the santoor on the national and international stage.

• He was known for his innovative playing style and his efforts to preserve the traditional music of Kashmir.

• He was also a composer and musicologist and established the SaMaPa (Sopori Academy of Music and Performing Arts) to promote Indian classical music.

questions.q_en: Ustad Hassu Khan, Ustad Haddu Khan and Ustad Nathu Khan were exponents of the ___________ Gharana.
questions.solution_en: The Gwalior Gharana evolved during the time of the Mughal Empire (1526 CE - 1857 CE). Among the early masters (ustad) were Naththan Khan, Naththan Pir Bakhsh and his grandsons Haddu, Hassu and Natthu Khan. The head musician in the imperial court was Bade Mohammad Khan, who was famous for his taanbazi style.
